summary.outcome: No reviewed first-party HLS family had enough public source-specific evidence to close third-party native playback. Catalogue permission statuses remain unchanged.

prototype_policy: Technically public HLS remains sufficient for native client-side playback unless recorded rights evidence requires link-out; pending direct streams stay visibly permission-pending.

families.reason: Tweede Kamer guidance documents Debat Direct, downloadable meeting fragments, and embeds for journalistic/media use under audiovisual-material licence terms, but it does not clearly authorize general public use of the catalogued raw HLS endpoints by a non-media catalogue.

TPchannel appears to be an official public parliamentary live/on-demand service operated by the National Assembly Radio and Television Broadcasting Station, but no source-specific reuse, embedding, or native-playback terms were found for the first-party HLS stream.

The HLS URL is hosted on the official Assembly domain, but standard TLS verification failed in the 2026-08-14 healthcheck and no source-specific reuse terms were found. General broadcaster-rights law reinforces caution but does not resolve catalogue permission.
